title: R’ Yose of Tzaytor
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Tanchuma, Kedoshim, R’ Berekhya said: An incident occurred in our town with a spirit dwelling at the spring. Another spirit came to confront it and sought to drive it away from there. A certain pious man was there, named R’ Yose of Tzaytor (Hyman reports the reading Abba Yose in Vayikra Rabbah, cited in the supplied Hebrew as the end of chapter 4). That spirit appeared to him and said, “Rabbi! For many years I have been here and have harmed no creature. This spirit has come upon me and seeks to drive me out of here and harm people.” He said to it, “What shall we do?” It said to him, “Take your staffs and your sickles and go out against it—and say, ‘Ours wins!’” They did so and drove it away from there.
Hyman reports that Midrash Tehillim, at the supplied locator פ״רז, relates the incident about Abba Yose ben Dokhtai.

notes.text: The second spirit comes to oppose the first. The chant “Ours wins” supports the resident spirit. The supplied Midrash Tehillim locator פ״רז remains unresolved; the Abba Yose variants are retained.

The supplied heading Yose and report-introducing Berekhya titles are abbreviated and remain R-prime; the spirit’s explicit full רבי! is preserved locally as Rabbi! without transfer to the heading. Berekhya’s our town, many years, no creature harmed, the resident spirit’s request against the newcomer, the genuine What shall we do? question, plural staffs and sickles, and the Ours wins chant remain. Confront renders the hostile encounter in this context without imposing a sexual coupling or independently proving physical combat. Gender alternates in Hyman’s spirit pronouns and remains unresolved by English it. Abba Yose and Abba Yose ben Dokhtai remain attributed variants, not merged identities. The Midrash Tehillim locator פ״רז is literal and unresolved; prior bounded chapter 20 nonmatch and search lead do not justify guessed 20:7 or global absence. No new whole primary scalar or print/history verification is claimed. All source holds remain.

The consulted Tanchuma parallels are Kedoshim 9 in both the Buber and Torat Emet texts. Hyman’s printed page (vol. II, p. 717) points to Vayikra Rabbah 24:3, which names Abba Yose of Tzaytor and gives a distinct version of the encounter at the spring. The consulted OYW Midrash Tehillim chapter 20 places the encounter in the days of Rabbi Abba bar Dosai. The Hyman print appears to give chapter 20 with a separate section number and a different name form from the supplied Hebrew. These citations document variant tellings and name forms.
